segments: [Book of the] Chronicle {OCR?}. 87.
Christian Greek kings,
of whom the first was Augustus and the last was Justin.
For although the language of the citizens and the laws was Greek,
yet the kings and the soldiers were Franks [i.e., Romans/Latins].
Now from this Tiberius onwards was the beginning of the second kingdom of the Greeks,
which was six hundred and two years after their former kingdom had ceased, which had begun from Caranus the Macedonian,
and ended with Perseus:
thirty-eight kings.
And in that year in which Tiberius began to reign,
which is the year eight hundred and ninety of the Greeks (579 of our Lord?):
Khosrow died.
And Hormizd his son reigned over the Persians for twelve years.
And he was arrogant and haughty, and did not send the token {symbolon} of the beginning of the reign,
according to the custom of the kings,
to the Romans.
Just as Tiberius also,
when he arose a few days before,
had sent a token {symbolon} to Khosrow.
And he stirred up war again in the land of Armenia.
Now Cyrus (Maurice?), the commander of the army of the Romans, prepared forces,
and in the brightness of the east he fell upon him like fire that is let loose in a forest.
And he laid them waste vehemently,
and the nobles and commanders of the Persians he bound.
And there was great consolation for the Romans.
For in these four years of the illness of Justin,
while Tiberius was governing the administration,
Queen Sophia would not allow the wife of Tiberius to enter the royal city.
And when Justin reproved her and said,
"It is a sin for you,
that while Tiberius is a young man and his body cannot endure continence,
you withhold his wife from him."
She, however, was saying,
"I have not lost my senses like you,
to give my kingdom away in my lifetime to another woman."
And thus, even after Justin died, Tiberius sought to bring in his wife,
and persuaded Sophia to command that she should come,
and not even then did she consent.
Then the Patriarch of the Chalcedonians incited Tiberius to abandon his wife,
and marry Sophia or her daughter.
Tiberius, however, severely rebuked that Patriarch and was indignant {OCR?},
and said:
"I will leave the kingdom,
and will not trample upon the Law."
He, however, made the excuse:
"The nobles compelled me to make you king, this being for the sake of peace."
